Script coverage from GT Unicode: Manipuri is Meitei Mayek 20/20; Santhali is Ol Chiki 19/20; Kashmiri and Urdu are Perso-Arabic 20/20 each.
Sindhi in the bench split is Devanagari, not Nastaliq; Nastaliq is covered only by Urdu + Kashmiri.

findings.claim: 224 of 400 pages are GT-thin (<200 chars) and excluded from SFT/DPO; 9 SFT lines have empty noisy_text; 6 queue pages unrankable (<2 engines producing tokens). South-400 assets are printed South-Indian pages, no handwriting.

SFT/DPO training assets are machine-engine OCR output vs PDF text layer pairs (noisy->gold) -- a post-correction/VLM SFT format usable for a post-correction stage; disagreement queue uses median pairwise token Jaccard.

B21 synthetic-lines spec (proto-100 B-21, DRAFT, 2026-09-30) targets ks (Nastaliq), sat (Ol Chiki), mni (Meitei Mayek): sat and mni have zero real clean pages in probe22 (0/100 clean under gates); ks severe fragmentation, surrogate Sarvam fails.

B21 hard rule: no text from Sarvam bench, Indic OCR Bench, IIIT-HW, IIIT-HW-words, BSTD or any public benchmark may be reused for synthetic text; gate G2 = grep for sarvam/indic-ocr-bench in product/synthetic/ must be empty.

B21 licensed text sources: Ol Chiki = Unicode CLDR + OLPC Santali corpus (~2k sentences); Nastaliq = URDU-KB / Rekhta PD subset filtered for Kashmiri lexicon (CC-BY-4.0/PD); Meitei Mayek = Manipuri Wikipedia + CLDR (CC-BY-SA, ~1.5k sentences). Corpus sizes are small relative to 5,000 lines/script target.
B21 fonts (all OFL-1.1): Noto Sans Ol Chiki 100% coverage, Noto Nastaliq Urdu 95% (Kashmiri subset, i.e. 5% glyph gap), Noto Sans Meetei Mayek 100%; Noto Sans fallback. Render with PyMuPDF.

B21 degradation pipeline (seed=20260926+line_id): font 12-24pt; DPI 150/200/300 weights 0.5/0.3/0.2; blur sigma Gamma(2,0.5) 0-1.5px; gaussian noise 0-15; salt-pepper 0-2%; contrast 0.5-1.5x; brightness +-30%; rotation +-3deg; skew +-5%; coffee stains Poisson(0.5) 0-3; fold lines 0-2; JPEG Q 40-95; Otsu/Sauvola.

B21 generator CLI and gates: python -m product.tools.gen_synthetic_lines --scripts ks,sat,mni --count 5000 --seed 20260926; gates G1 license audit, G2 no bench text, G3 byte-identical determinism, G4 >=5,000 lines per script + 100 samples human-reviewed. Tool is spec only (no evidence it exists/ran).

B21 spec contains defects: example Kashmiri text field mixes Devanagari (bॅनٛوٛ) into Perso-Arabic string; license row 'synthetic_pd_unicode' while Wikipedia source is CC-BY-SA (share-alike conflicts with PD label); two sections numbered 7; two G4 rows; spec covers only printed-line synthesis (no handwriting, no R4 scan restoration beyond generic aging).

SFT split 80/10/10 per language by hash(image_id)%10 (train 160, val 20, test 20 total); note: split is over PAGES from only 2 PDFs per language, so val/test are same-source-PDF pages (not independent writers/books) -- leakage-by-source risk acknowledged.

Training pairs are full printed PAGES with avg GT 2308 chars (kok; min152 max4011) and 1744 (pa; min940 max2409), capped at 1024 chars with truncation risk; page-level SFT on 80 images/lang is tiny (n=80), with memorisation risk acknowledged.

Primary 200 paired (kok100+pa100), secondary 160 held-out. Qlora vs zero-shot Qwen2.5-VL-3B wrap baseline.

Eval spec internal inconsistency: 'validation 160 items (80 per lang)' conflated with the 80/10/10 split; resolved by 200 paired items on FULL probe22 set -- which INCLUDES the 160 train images (the McNemar on 100/lang is not held-out; only 20/lang is). Pseudocode evaluates on {lang}_sft.jsonl (all 100 incl. train).
